tasks.short: Organize and lead games, crafts, music, stories and field trips.

steps.what: Open the group's physical, mental and social development goals
Organize activities designed to promote physical, mental and social development, such as games, crafts, music, storytelling and field trips
Lead those activities with the children in the room
Note which activities ran, which development goal they served, and any material that was short

tasks.design: The {OTHER} pupil record opens this group's physical, mental and social goals for the week. The pedagogical lead keeps each goal as a code, a short text and a week; a missing goal is typed in that open step. The preschool teacher still organizes the games, crafts, music, storytelling or field trip, and still leads it. Afterwards, fixed fields store the activity name, the goal it served and any material that was short.
tasks.previous_blocker: The week's goals sat in a plan book the teacher already knew. A drafted activity would not know who is tired, absent or new that morning.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning-goal tracking already sits on the pupil record, so the three development goals can be stored on the group without a new store. Native fields are configured before any custom code.
tasks.still_hard: Leading the game, reading the room, and a field trip's headcount, permission and the walk itself.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher sees which children can join this activity today. A goal code does not.

ambition.what: Each morning the teacher can see which physical, mental or social goal this group has not touched this week, and still chooses the activity.

tasks.altitude: The games, crafts, songs and stories stay. The goal list is open before the teacher chooses, and the choice stays with the teacher.

reach.task: Keep the group's physical, mental and social goals for the week
reach.learn: Which goal code was missing, so the teacher typed it before organizing the activity

evidence.claim: ParnasSys keeps pupil records and learning-goal tracking, and names no AI. That is the store these development goals use.
Model knowledge: the teacher still organizes and still leads the activity. A goal list does not know which children are in the room.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this task starts when the teacher looks up the week's goals and ends when the activity note is stored. It does not draft a lesson, score a child or book a trip.

Structured input, group goal list. Producer: the pedagogical lead. Fields: group id, goal code (physical, mental or social), goal text, week. Fallback: the teacher types those fields inside s1, and that typing sits in the remaining 50 percent.
The activity note is produced here, after the activity, by this teacher. Fields: group id, date, activity name, goal code, material short. Nothing reads that note until it exists.

Mechanism for s1: the goal code opens the week's list instead of a hunt through the plan book. Mechanism for s4: the goal code chosen in s2 is picked from that list, and the activity name and the short material go in fixed fields instead of a blank page. s2 and s3 are not shortened.
Test the pupil record's own goal fields before custom code. Upkeep is retiring a goal code when the lead changes the week, about 0.3 hour per 100 hours of this task.
unknowns: Whether this group keeps goals in a pupil record or only in a paper plan book.
Whether a field trip needs a separate parent permission that this note does not cover.
research_questions: On a repeated game, how much of the teacher's time is the choice and the leading, and how much is the note afterwards?

already_counted.description: Read the open goal list and type a goal the lead has not entered.
Fill the activity note after the activity and correct a goal code that does not match what ran.

incremental.description: Retire a goal code when the pedagogical lead changes the week's list.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A repeated game the teacher already knows. The goal list is open, and the note is a few fields. The teacher still organizes and still leads. A field trip still needs the permission, the headcount and the walk, which this design does not shorten.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Identify signs of problems and discuss them with parents and specialists.

steps.what: Open the last note on this child's emotional, developmental or health-related problems
Identify children showing signs of emotional, developmental or health-related problems
Discuss those signs with supervisors, parents or guardians and child development specialists
Record the signs discussed and who among the supervisors, parents, guardians or specialists was told

tasks.design: Nothing flags a child. The teacher identifies emotional, developmental or health-related signs in the room, then discusses them with the supervisor, the parent or guardian, and the child development specialist. Before the talk, the {OTHER} pupil record opens the last note this teacher wrote. After the talk, fixed fields store what was seen, the type the teacher named, and who was told. A first concern starts from blank fields. No camera and no model names a feeling.
tasks.previous_blocker: A sign is seen in the moment. A model that named an emotion from a camera or from a note would be doing the identifying.
tasks.enabler_now: Once this teacher has written a note, the child id can open it. Parent and pupil participation on pupil-data rules is the consent step, not a works-council route, because that route does not apply to schools.
tasks.still_hard: The conversation itself, and not treating a bad morning as a problem.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher decides whether the sign is new, and says it to the parent in the room. The record only stores what was already said.
tasks.altitude: The teacher still decides whether a sign is a bad morning or a problem, and still has the conversation. The last note is open beforehand. Nothing flags the child.

reach.task: Hear the sign the teacher brings from the room
reach.learn: Which sign was only clear in the discussion and had no earlier note

reach.task: Talk with the teacher about the sign
reach.learn: Which health detail the parent has not given the school, so the note must not invent it

evidence.claim: Inferring pupils' emotions is a prohibited practice, so this design does not name an emotional problem from a camera or a model.

The school participation act gives parents and pupils a say on pupil-data rules, and gives staff a say on tools that can monitor staff. A works council act does not apply to schools. This note is pupil data the teacher writes, not a monitor on the teacher.
Model knowledge: the teacher identifies the sign in the room and discusses it. A stored note does not see the child.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this task starts when the teacher opens the last note and ends when today's concern note is stored. It does not send a message, score the child or call a specialist by itself.

Structured input, last concern note. Producer: this teacher, at the previous s4 of this task. Fields: child id, date, what was seen, problem type the teacher named (emotional, developmental or health-related), who was told, follow-up date. Fallback: blank fields inside s1, and that typing sits in the remaining 50 percent. A new sign is identified in s2, not pre-filled.
Health wording can be special-category data. It stays in the pupil record. No model drafts it.

Mechanism for s1: the child id opens the last note instead of a hunt through a notebook. Mechanism for s4: who was told and the date are fixed fields; the sentence about what was seen is still typed by the teacher. s2 and s3 stay at full time.

Parent and pupil participation comes before these fields are switched on. Until then the notebook stays and s1 is a notebook lookup at full time. Upkeep is about 0.3 hour per 100 hours of this task, for a follow-up date that has passed.
unknowns: Whether this setting is a school covered by the school participation act, or childcare with different parent rules.
Who may read a health-related note besides the teacher and the specialist.
research_questions: How often is the first note on a child blank, because nobody has written a concern before?

already_counted.description: Read the last concern note, or type the blank fields when this is the first one.
Write what was seen and who was told, after the discussion, and fix a type that does not match what was said.

incremental.description: Close a follow-up date that passed with no new conversation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A child who already has a note. The teacher still identifies the sign and still has the conversation. Only the opening and the fields are shorter. A first concern is typed from blank fields, and the talk is the whole task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain the student records the laws and school policies require.

steps.what: See which children are present and which guardian collects them
Open the pupil fields the student records must hold
Decide what is accurate and complete for these student records
Maintain accurate and complete student records required by laws, district policies and administrative regulations

tasks.design: At the door the teacher still sees who is present and who collects the child, and that attendance mark is the capture. The {OTHER} pupil record then opens the fields the school requires, using the enrolment the administrator keeps and any activity note or concern note this teacher has already written. The teacher decides what is accurate, types anything still empty, and confirms that text. The screen does not invent an attendance mark or a concern.
tasks.previous_blocker: The official file did not know who walked in the door. Copying a day into prose was the record.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil records and learning-goal tracking already exist in a pupil administration. Required fields can be configured there before any custom code. Parents and pupils have a say on those pupil-data rules.
tasks.still_hard: Judging what is accurate, a medical note the parent has not given, and a day with an incident that must be written in the teacher's words.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher knows who was in the room and what is fair to write. The file only holds what the teacher confirms.
tasks.altitude: The door is unchanged. Required fields are already on the child. The teacher still decides what is accurate, and still confirms the record.

reach.task: Keep the enrolment the teacher opens at the door
reach.learn: Which guardian, collection rule or medical note was empty when the child arrived

evidence.claim: ParnasSys keeps pupil records, an individual plan module and learning-goal tracking, and names no AI. The daily record uses that pupil file, not a drafted comment.

Parents and pupils have a say on pupil-data rules under the school participation act. Staff consent applies to tools that can monitor staff. This screen stores what the teacher types. It does not monitor the teacher. A works council act does not apply to schools.
Model knowledge: attendance is still marked by the teacher who sees the child. A query does not know who was in the room.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this task starts at the door and ends when the teacher confirms today's student record. It does not write a support plan, send a parent message or score the child.

Structured input, enrolment record. Producer: the school administrator. Fields: child id, preferred name, guardian names, who may collect, medical note the parent supplied, start date. Fallback: the teacher asks at the door (that asking is inside s1 at full time) and types the missing field inside s2.

Structured input, attendance mark. Producer: this teacher at s1. Fields: child id, date, present yes or no, who collected the child, time. Capture time is s1 at remaining 100. If the mark is on paper, the teacher copies the tick inside s4, and that copy sits in the remaining 50 percent.

Structured input, activity note. Producer: this teacher after the activity, in the activity task. Fields: activity name, goal code, date. Fallback: leave the activity field blank and type it in s4 if the teacher decides it belongs in today's record. No activity is invented.
Structured input, concern note. Producer: this teacher after the discussion, in the concern task. If none exists, s4 does not create a concern.

Mechanism for s2: the child id opens enrolment and any note already stored, instead of assembling the day from slips. Mechanism for s4: those stored fields fill the record, and the teacher types only the free line, then confirms. s1 and s3 stay at full time.
s3 decides the facts. s4 writes that text, including any edit, and the confirm binds that exact text. A later edit needs a new confirm.
Parent and pupil participation comes before the screen is switched on. Upkeep is about 0.5 hour per 100 hours of this task, when a required field is added or retired.
unknowns: Which fields this school's policy actually requires on a preschool day.
Whether the door mark is ticked in the pupil record or on paper.
Whether a support-plan deadline applies in this setting. This task does not draft one.
research_questions: On a calm day, which record fields are already filled from the door and from enrolment, and which are still a sentence the teacher writes?

already_counted.description: Check the open student record for a missing enrolment field, a missing attendance mark or a blank activity line.
Type the free line, copy a paper attendance tick when that is how the door was marked, and confirm the student record.

incremental.description: Add or retire a required field when district policy or the school rule changes.

approvals.approved_version: Student record on screen at confirm: attendance and collector from the door, enrolment from the administrator, activity or concern only when this teacher already wrote them, plus any edit made before confirm.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A calm day where attendance was ticked at the door in the pupil record, enrolment is complete, and there is no incident. The teacher still does the door and still decides what is accurate. A paper door list or an incident keeps the writing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe and evaluate performance, behavior, development and health.

steps.what: Open the last watch-point for this child's development and physical health
Observe children's performance, behavior, social development and physical health
Evaluate that performance, behavior, social development and physical health
Record the evaluation of performance, behavior, social development and physical health in the teacher's words

tasks.design: The teacher still observes and still evaluates performance, behavior, social development and physical health in the room. The {OTHER} pupil record opens the watch-point this teacher saved last time: child, area, what to watch, date. A first day is blank fields, typed in that open step. After the evaluation the teacher writes their own sentence in those fields and can save the next watch-point. The screen does not suggest a score, a label or a feeling.
tasks.previous_blocker: The evaluation is the watching. A suggested score would be a second judgement the teacher did not make, and a camera that inferred a feeling is not allowed.
tasks.enabler_now: The last watch-point can reopen by child id once this teacher has saved one. Native fields on the pupil record come before any custom code.
tasks.still_hard: The child in the room, and not turning a note into a diagnosis or a level.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher sees the performance and decides what it means. The record keeps that sentence. It does not produce one.
tasks.altitude: Watching and evaluating stay in the room, at the same length. The last watch-point is open. The teacher still writes the sentence. Nothing changes about who may evaluate a child.

reach.task: Read the evaluation note when the teacher asks for a second look
reach.learn: Which sentence was a watch-point and not a score, so the lead does not treat it as a level

evidence.claim: Annex III point 3 treats AI that evaluates learning outcomes as high-risk. This design does not score performance, behavior or development.
Inferring pupils' emotions is prohibited. This design does not infer a feeling from behavior or from physical health.
Model knowledge: a note on a child's physical health can be special-category data. The teacher writes it. No model drafts it.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this task starts when the teacher opens the last watch-point and ends when today's evaluation note is stored. It does not set a level, admit a pupil or watch a test.

Structured input, watch-point. Producer: this teacher, at the previous s4. Fields: child id, area (performance, behavior, social development or physical health), what to watch next, date. Fallback: blank fields inside s1, typed inside the remaining 50 percent. The watch-point does not contain a score.
The evaluation sentence is produced in s3 by the teacher and only then stored in s4. s4 does not draft it.

Mechanism for s1: the child id opens the last watch-point instead of a hunt through notes. Mechanism for s4: child, area and date fill from that watch-point, and the teacher still types the sentence. s2 and s3 stay at full time.
Parent and pupil participation comes before these fields are switched on. Upkeep is about 0.3 hour per 100 hours of this task, to drop a watch-point the teacher no longer uses.
unknowns: Whether anyone besides the teacher is expected to read the evaluation note.
Whether physical-health notes are stored in this pupil record or in a separate medical file.
research_questions: How often does the teacher start from a saved watch-point, and how often is the page blank because yesterday had no note?

already_counted.description: Read the open watch-point, or type a blank one on a first day.
Type the evaluation sentence in the teacher's words and save the next watch-point.

incremental.description: Drop a watch-point the teacher no longer uses.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A child with a watch-point from yesterday. The teacher still observes every child and still evaluates. Only the page-finding and the repeated name and date are shorter. A blank day, or a sentence that takes thought, keeps almost all of the time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teacher still leads the activity, still notices the child, still evaluates, and still talks with the parent. The pupil record opens the goal, the last note and the required fields before those acts. No model picks the game, names a problem or scores a child.
reach: Pedagogical lead: which physical, mental or social goal was missing, so the morning list could not open.
School administrator: which enrolment field, guardian or medical note was empty when the child arrived.
Child development specialist: which sign was discussed in the room and written only afterwards.
Parent or guardian: which collection rule or health note the school did not have.
skills_to_grow: Reject an activity that does not fit the children who are in the room today.
Reject a record that states a problem the teacher did not see.
Reject a note that adds a label the conversation with the parent did not use.
role.ambitious_version: Each morning the goals and the last watch-point are already on the screen, and the teacher spends the time in the activity and with the child. A concern is still seen and still discussed before anyone writes it. The teacher still decides.
